title: A merge with conflicts in both test and product files has a role that can land it
why: Lane doing-needs-live-lane (#1340, F3) merged main and hit conflicts in test and product files. A builder may not commit a merge that touches a test file, and a test-author may not commit product files, so no role could land it; the lane orchestrator committed it itself (head 36c08a00e). Source: coordinator 17:50 CST Nov 6.
note:
Incident, Nov 7 12:30-13:05 CST (lane cs-revive-ready): merging origin/main into reviewed draft PRs whose conflicts span test and product files. builder-test-edit refused the builders' test-file writes, and test-authors cannot write product files, so no single role could commit the merge. Hit on #1143, #1175, #1179 and #1166; #1317 needed a separate test-author fix after the merge was pushed. EnterWorktree into a sibling agent's worktree is refused, and a builder that aborts loses its resolutions. Route used: each role saves its resolved files under the lane's scratchpad, and the lane session copies both sets into one merge commit in its own worktree, then runs the touched suites through verdict. Cost: about 2 extra agent spawns and 1 extra merge per PR. No new debt (coordinator).
Give mixed-conflict merges a route that keeps red then green, e.g. the test-author commits the test side, then the builder commits the merge. Sighting (lane record-after-each-round, session_013NEJL3gDkEvHawhJUPygWa, 15:29 CST Nov 8; it proposed step merge-conflict-role-split, folded here): merging main into #1678 at 15:28 CST gave conflicts in test and product files. builder-test-edit refused the builder on the test file; test-author-scope refused the test author on the product file, with no override; agent isolation kept each from the other's worktree. Workaround today: the coordinator's split merge (owner item 420 a): the builder merges main, resolves product files, keeps the branch's test file and commits; a test author then adds main's test changes in its own commit; the in-between head is never handed off.
